scenes: March twenty thirteen. Bitcoin split into two chains.
And the developers chose to kill the newer one.
It started with an update. Version zero point eight was brand new, but many computers still ran zero point seven.
Then one huge block arrived. It touched over five thousand transactions.
The new computers accepted it. The old ones choked.
It needed over ten thousand database locks. The old version ran out.
Now there were two Bitcoins at the same time.
Mount Gox and Bit Pay shut down deposits.
And the price dropped twenty-four percent.
So developers asked the big miners to go back to the old version.
About six hours later, the old chain took the lead, and won.
And someone spent the same ten thousand dollars twice, against Oh Kay Pay.
One block. Two Bitcoins. Bug, or warning?
